title: InfoDCL: Informative Noise Enhanced Diffusion Based Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Recommendation data are sparse, limiting the semantic information captured by contrastive-learning views.

gap.claim: Existing methods randomly perturb interaction graphs without access to authentic user preferences, producing insufficiently informative views.

contributions.claim: InfoDCL is a diffusion-based contrastive learning framework for recommendation that generates contrastive views using noise integrated with auxiliary semantic information and user-preference signals.
InfoDCL uses a collaborative training objective to turn mutual interference between generation and preference learning into collaboration.
Multiple GCN layers are used only during inference to incorporate higher-order co-occurrence information while maintaining training efficiency.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe InfoDCL as a novel framework and propose a novel paradigm for applying diffusion methods in contrastive learning frameworks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets are reported to show that InfoDCL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that InfoDCL enhances recommendation performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contrastive learning has shown promise in recommender systems.
Random graph perturbation lacks authentic preference information and captures insufficient semantic information in sparse recommendation data.
InfoDCL uses informative noise, diffusion-based preference generation, and generated contrastive views.
A collaborative objective coordinates generation and preference learning, while inference-time GCN layers add higher-order co-occurrence information.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art methods across five real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Random perturbations may be uninformative when interaction data are sparse and authentic preferences are unavailable.

interpretation.claim: Contrastive views can benefit from perturbations informed by semantic or preference-related signals.

application.claim: In recommender systems, investigate diffusion-based view generation that incorporates auxiliary semantic information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond recommendation or across other data regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, evaluation metrics, baseline details, or numerical results.
The abstract does not specify the auxiliary semantic information or diffusion-process implementation details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, causal effects, or reproducibility.
